title: Per-tenant surge forgiveness window and invoice explainability
creator: Leah Park
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated fleets see transient token/throughput spikes that push them into overage charges even when the spike is short (seconds-to-minutes). Current billing is per-minute aggregation and attributes every exceeded second to overage, which leads to surprise invoices. We need a deterministic, auditable policy that: 1) defines a per-tenant forgiveness window for transient capacity overshoots, 2) calculates a human-readable invoice adjustment explanation, and 3) exposes adjustments and rationale in Console and billing exports.

Goals:
- Define a forgiveness window parameter (configurable per-tenant) that groups short overshoots and optionally discounts them from overage billing.
- Create a deterministic allocation algorithm that prorates temporary top-ups across requests and time and creates line-item adjustments rather than opaque credits.
- Surface the calculation in Console (per-route breakdown + example request traces) and include CSV export columns for audit teams.
- Ensure the approach preserves SLO assurances for other tenants and cannot be gamed by malicious traffic patterns.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change base pricing or committed capacity products. It focuses on how we account for brief overshoots and present them on invoices.

High-level design decisions: 
1) Forgiveness window semantics: a sliding window measured in seconds (default 180s) where transient surge that returns below committed capacity before window expiry is eligible for forgiveness. Customer teams can set window to 0 (no forgiveness) or up to 900s.
2) Eligibility criteria: forgiveness applies only if (a) average per-tenant queue time and tail latency remain within SLO during the window, and (b) the tenant was not throttling other tenants (cross-tenant interference metric).
3) Accounting model: instead of full metering cancellation, we create an "Adjustment" ledger entry that documents: window start/end, raw overage usage, forgiveness fraction, applied discount, and audit trace links. Adjustments are additive and appear as separate line items on invoices (not negative token deletions).
4) Safety controls: a daily cap on forgivable tokens per tenant (configurable), a global operator throttle, and anomaly detection to block forgiveness for patterns that look like repeated short spikes.

Telemetry & Metrics:
- forgiveness.window_seconds (per-tenant)
- forgiveness.eligible_overage_tokens
- forgiveness.applied_tokens
- forgiveness.rejections.reason (rate-limited)
- invoice.adjustment.count and invoice.adjustment.total_tokens

Console UX:
- Billing -> Adjustments tab (per-month) listing adjustment entries with explainability fields and link to route traces.
- Route-level toggle to enable/disable forgiveness and a slider to set window seconds.
- Example calculation modal showing step-by-step prorating for a representative 4-minute spike.

Algorithm (example):
1) Detect overage event E for tenant T: capture time window [t0,t1].
2) If (t1 - t0) <= forgiveness_window and eligibility checks pass: compute raw_overage_tokens = sum(tokens_exceeding_commit during [t0,t1]).
3) Compute decay_weighted_prorate across requests so heavy long-running requests don't get fully forgiven: applied_forgiveness = min(raw_overage_tokens, tenant_daily_forgive_cap - today_forgiven).
4) Create ledger adjustment: {tenant, start, end, raw_overage_tokens, applied_forgiveness, reason_code, links}.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (backend prototype): implement detection and ledger adjustment generator in billing service; add metrics and a feature flag. (ENG work + billing team collaboration).
- Phase 2 (safety): add per-tenant caps, anomaly detector rules in streaming pipeline.
- Phase 3 (UX): Console list, modal, and export columns; include sample traces from Trace Store.
- Phase 4 (rollout): Start with opt-in for beta tenants, iterate based on disputes and telemetry, then enable default with conservative window.

Edge cases & trade-offs:
- We could suppress overage entirely for eligible events, but that hides usage and breaks auditability. Choosing adjustments keeps raw usage intact for SLO and capacity planning.
- Forgiveness could be exploited by scripted short spikes; mitigations include daily caps and anomaly detection.
- Per-tenant windows add operational complexity; default stays small (180s) and most customers will not change it.

Open questions:
- Should forgiveness reduce chargeable tokens or only produce an adjustment credit? Preferred: adjustment credit because it preserves raw metrics.
- Is a decay-weighted prorate fair across different request types (chat vs embeddings)? We need to validate with billing simulations across representative workloads.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Backend can produce adjustment ledger entries for a synthetic set of overage events (unit + integration tests).
- Console shows adjustment entries and a trace link for each.
- Billing export CSV contains adjustment columns and the numbers match ledger.
- No SLO regressions or cross-tenant interference during beta (monitoring guardrails pass).

2025-01-30 - Leah Park: Legal reviewed line-item approach; prefers adjustments over token deletion. No blocking issues but asked for clear language in invoices explaining what an adjustment is.
